content: 1. Meclizine and Thalidomide: Co-administration of meclizine and thalidomide increases sedation. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of excessive central nervous system (CNS) depression. 2. Meclizine and Alfentanil: Both drugs increase sedation. It is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Limit use to patients for whom alternative treatment options are inadequate. 3. Meclizine and Buprenorphine: Co-administration increases sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. This combination should only be used in patients with no adequate alternative treatment options. 4. Meclizine and Buprenorphine Buccal: Both drugs increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Limit use to patients for whom alternative treatments are insufficient. 5. Meclizine and Codeine: The combination of these drugs increases sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Use should be limited to patients without adequate alternative options. 6. Meclizine and Hydrocodone: Both drugs increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Limit use to patients for whom alternative treatments are inadequate. 7. Meclizine and Hydromorphone: Co-administration increases sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. This combination should only be used in patients with no adequate alternative treatment options. 8. Meclizine and Morphine: Both drugs increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Limit use to patients for whom alternative treatments are insufficient. 9. Meclizine and Olopatadine (Intranasal): Co-administration increases the risk of CNS depression, leading to additive impairment of psychomotor performance and daytime functioning. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Meclizine and Oxycodone: Both drugs increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Limit use to patients for whom alternative treatments are inadequate. 11. Meclizine and Oxymorphone: Co-administration increases sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. This combination should only be used in patients with no adequate alternative treatment options. 12. Meclizine and Pramlintide: The combination of these drugs results in synergistic inhibition of gastrointestinal motility. This combination is contraindicated. 13. Meclizine and Remifentanil: Both drugs increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Limit use to patients for whom alternative treatments are insufficient. 14. Meclizine and Ropinirole: Co-administration increases the risk of additive neuropsychiatric side effects. Avoid use and monitor patients receiving this combination for signs of excessive CNS toxicity. 15. Meclizine and Secretin: Meclizine decreases the effects of secretin through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Discontinue anticholinergic drugs at least five half-lives before administering secretin. 16. Meclizine and Sofpironium (Topical): Co-administration may result in additive anticholinergic adverse effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Meclizine and Zuranolone: Co-administration with other CNS depressants may increase impairment of psychomotor performance or CNS depressant effects. If unavoidable, consider dose reduction. 18. Meclizine and AbobotulinumtoxinA: Meclizine may potentiate the effects of botulinum toxin, leading to excessive neuromuscular weakness and heightened systemic anticholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Meclizine and Acetaminophen/Phenyltoloxamine: Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Meclizine and Aclidinium: Both drugs decrease cholinergic effects or transmission. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Meclizine and Acrivastine: Co-administration increases sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Meclizine and Alprazolam: Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Meclizine and Amantadine: Co-administration may result in increased anticholinergic adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Meclizine and Amifampridine: Meclizine increases the toxicity of amifampridine, which may lead to seizures. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 25. Meclizine and Amisulpride: Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Meclizine and Amitriptyline: Co-administration decreases cholinergic effects and increases sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Meclizine and Amobarbital: Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Meclizine and Amoxapine: Co-administration decreases cholinergic effects and increases sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Meclizine and Anticholinergic/Sedative Combinations: Co-administration decreases cholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Meclizine and Aripiprazole: Meclizine decreases the levels of aripiprazole by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Meclizine and Asenapine: Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Meclizine and Atropine: Co-administration decreases cholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Meclizine and Avapritinib: Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Meclizine and Baclofen: Co-administration increases sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Meclizine and Belladonna Alkaloids: Co-administration decreases cholinergic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Meclizine and Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Meclizine and Benztropine: Co-administration decreases cholinergic effects and may result in additive anticholinergic adverse effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Meclizine and Bethanechol: Bethanechol increases cholinergic effects, while meclizine decreases them. The effect of this interaction is unclear. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Meclizine and Brexanolone: Co-administration increases sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Meclizine and Brexpiprazole: Both drugs increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely.
